guide.title: Redbridge, London: Wanstead Park, Valentines Mansion, Ilford Hospital Chapel and Hainault Forest
guide.intro: Redbridge is an outer London borough east of the Roding, and it reads as four places rather than one. Wanstead and Snaresbrook hold the heritage core: a 161.74-hectare registered landscape left from a vanished mansion, with its Grade II Temple and Grotto still standing in it, and a Jacobean Gothic orphanage of 1841 working as a Crown Court since 1974. Ilford, Gants Hill and Valentines carry the town centre, a house of 1696 in a 51.52-hectare registered park, and a chapel founded about 1130 on Ilford Hill. Woodford runs a ridge of greens and parish churches with two listed monuments facing each other across the High Road. Barkingside, Fairlop and Hainault give the borough its country parks. The National Heritage List for England records 138 listed-building entries inside the borough: 1 at Grade I, 12 at Grade II* and 125 at Grade II, and no scheduled monuments at all.

sections.heading: Wanstead and Snaresbrook
sections.body:
The south-west corner of the borough is its heritage core, and everything in it sits on the Central line between Leytonstone and South Woodford.

Wanstead Park is entered from Warren Road, E11 2LT. It was registered at Grade II* on 1 October 1987 as NHLE 1000194, and Historic England records the registered area as 161.74 hectares; the managed municipal park inside that boundary is about 140 acres, or 57 hectares. The City of London Corporation bought the park in 1880 from Henry Wellesley, 1st Earl Cowley, and administers it as part of Epping Forest, having been Conservator of the forest since the Epping Forest Act 1878. The Corporation describes it as "once a formal landscape surrounding the great Wanstead House, often compared to Blenheim Palace"; the house is gone and the park remains. It publishes the Chestnut Trail as a circular walk through the park, fishing at Perch Pond and the Ornamental Waters, and a bluebell season in Chalet Wood from March to May, with visitors asked to keep to the marked paths. It publishes no general opening hours for the park, so none are given here.

The Temple stands inside the park and is listed Grade II as NHLE 1081016, first listed 20 December 1954. It is one of the Corporation's Epping Forest visitor centres — "once a rich man's folly, and now home to art and history exhibitions and the story of Wanstead Park" — and it holds the story of the park's Roman villa told through mosaics and other items from the Epping Forest museum collection, together with statues that once stood through the grounds. It opens 11am to 3pm on published open days: in 2026, Sunday 15 March; Saturday 11 and Sunday 12 April; Saturday 25 and Sunday 26 April; Saturday 9 and Sunday 10 May; Saturday 13 and Sunday 14 June; Saturday 11 and Sunday 12 July; Saturday 8 and Sunday 9 August; Saturday 12 and Sunday 13 September; Sunday 11 October; Sunday 15 November; and Sunday 13 December. Entrance is free on those days and tours are available for a fee. There is a gift shop, ground-floor exterior toilets including a RADAR-key accessible unisex unit, and a small Blue Badge car park reached from Warren Road; both floors have ground-level access, and the main entrance is up a resin-bonded path on a steep incline with two shallow steps.

The Grotto, listed Grade II as NHLE 1183624 on the same day in 1954, stands on the bank of the Ornamental Waters about 270 m from the E11 2LT postcode unit, at national grid reference TQ 41926 87480. It is a surviving garden structure of the Wanstead House estate, a roofless shell that is seen from the lakeside path rather than entered. It is a separate list entry from the two grottoes at Valentines Park in Ilford, NHLE 1244052 and NHLE 1183617, which are different structures in a different park.

On Overton Drive, E11 2LW, the Church of St Mary the Virgin was listed Grade I on 20 December 1954 as NHLE 1081008; the National Heritage List for England records one Grade I entry inside the borough and this is it. The parish is first recorded in 1208, and the medieval church was replaced 70 feet to the north by the present building between 1787 and 1790, on a plot given by James Tylney-Long. Thomas Hardwick designed it, the foundation stone was laid on 13 July 1787, and the church was completed on 24 June 1790, consecrated by Beilby Porteus, Bishop of London. The monument to Josiah Child was moved in when its medieval predecessor was demolished. The sculptor Joseph Wilton and Vice-Admiral Robert Plampin are buried in the churchyard, and both memorials carry their own Grade II entries, NHLE 1183582 and NHLE 1390858. The churchyard railings and gates are Grade II, NHLE 1357970, and the pair of gatepiers at the entrance to Overton Drive are Grade II*, NHLE 1081022. The parish now shares its ministry with Christ Church, Wanstead, Grade II*, NHLE 1081017. No source states the church's opening hours, so none are given here.

Snaresbrook Crown Court, at 75 Hollybush Hill, E11 1QW, was listed Grade II on 11 November 1968 as NHLE 1358004, the entry amended on 12 December 2019. George Gilbert Scott and William Bonython Moffatt built it in 1841-1843 in Jacobean Gothic for the Infant Orphan Asylum, founded by the philanthropist Andrew Reed. It remained an orphanage until 1938, then the Royal Wanstead School until 1971, and was converted to a Crown Court for £1.6m in 1973, opening as a court on 26 November 1974. It runs 20 court rooms, handles about 7,000 cases a year, is a third-tier centre and is one of twelve serving Greater London. It stands in 18 acres of grounds with its own lake, Eagle Pond, opposite the junction of Hollybush Hill and Wanstead High Street. It is a working court, read from Hollybush Hill, with no visitor route through the building. The former gatekeeper's lodge, NHLE 1467326, and the former indoor swimming pool, NHLE 1467344, were both added to the list at Grade II on 3 December 2019, fifty-one years after the main building.

sections.heading: Ilford, Gants Hill and Valentines
sections.body:
Ilford is the borough's town centre and carries its National Rail and Elizabeth line corridor. Valentines Mansion, with its registered park around it, stands 1,463 m from Ilford station and 506 m from Gants Hill on the Central line.

Valentines Mansion, on Emerson Road, IG1 4XA, was listed Grade II* on 10 April 1954 as NHLE 1081014 and stands in the Valentines Mansion conservation area. It was built in 1696 for Lady Tillotson, widow of John Tillotson, Archbishop of Canterbury, and Vision RCL, the registered charity that manages it for Redbridge Council, describes over 320 years of history on the site. Entry is free, and the operator opens the house twice a week, on Sundays and Mondays: 12pm to 5pm from March to October and 11am to 3pm from November to February. No dogs are admitted except guide dogs. The period rooms shown to visitors include the Drawing Room, Morning Room, Regency Parlour, Bedchamber, Victorian Kitchen and Grand Staircase, and the grounds hold the Old English Garden and the Walled Garden, with the Gardener's Cottage Cafe beside the house. Seven further structures in the immediate grounds carry their own entries at two different grades: the railings, gates and gatepiers to Valentines Park are Grade II*, NHLE 1081027, while the dovecote and attached garden walls, NHLE 1081015, the canal-head grotto, NHLE 1183617, a second grotto, NHLE 1244052, the ha-ha, NHLE 1244054, the sundial, NHLE 1244053, and the Gardener's Cottage, NHLE 1360821, are each Grade II.

Valentines Park, entered from Cranbrook Road, IG1 4TG, was registered at Grade II on 1 October 1987 as NHLE 1000843, and Historic England records the registered area as 51.52 hectares. It was laid out as the grounds of the mansion, holds a Green Flag Award, and contains a 300-year-old field maple, ornamental gardens, flowering meadows, two children's play areas and two cafes — the Gardener's Cottage Cafe by the mansion and Valentines Park Cafe by the bandstand. Its outdoor gym carries 15 pieces of equipment across 20 work stations. The park's boundary railings, gates and gatepiers were listed Grade II* in their own right on 10 April 1954, NHLE 1081027.

Redbridge Museum and Heritage Centre occupies the second floor of Redbridge Central Library on Clements Road, IG1 1EA, about 400 m from Ilford station. Arts Council England records one Accredited museum inside the borough: this one holds Full Accreditation, with Vision Redbridge Culture & Leisure as its governing body and Local Authority as its museum type. The museum opens Tuesday to Saturday, 11am to 5pm, and states that it explores "the many different places, people and events in over 200,000 years of Redbridge history"; its permanent exhibition reopened in August 2024 after a redevelopment. The Heritage Centre is the borough's archive and local studies service, open Tuesday to Friday and every other Saturday, 10.30am to 4pm, holding material on the history of Ilford, Wanstead, Woodford and Redbridge with free local and family history resources.

Ilford Hospital Chapel, on Ilford Hill, IG1 2AT, is formally the Hospital Chapel of St Mary the Virgin and St Thomas of Canterbury, an almshouse foundation dating from about 1130. The chapel was listed Grade II* on 10 April 1954 as NHLE 1300587 and the entry was amended on 20 June 2003; the almshouses, NHLE 1390507, and the chaplain's house, NHLE 1390508, were added to the list at Grade II on 20 June 2003, nearly fifty years after the chapel itself. It stands on Ilford Hill above the Roding, about 22 m from the IG1 2AT postcode unit and about 135 m south of Ilford station. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.

sections.heading: Woodford, South Woodford and Claybury
sections.body:
The northern ridge carries large greens, ancient parish churches and Churchill's old constituency, and runs out at Claybury into 70 hectares of Green Flag parkland around the shell of a Victorian asylum.

The Statue of Winston Churchill stands on the green beside the High Road at Woodford Green, IG8 9HF, and was listed Grade II on 19 January 2016 as NHLE 1430402, under the entry name "Statue of Winston Churchill (and plinth)". David McFall made the bronze in 1958-59 and it was erected in 1959. It commemorates Churchill's service as member for the Woodford constituency: he was elected for Epping in 1924, held the new Woodford seat from 1945 and stood down in 1964. The green is open at any hour.

About 1.5 km north along the same High Road, at IG8 0RD, the Anti-Air War Memorial faces it — a stone bomb on a plinth, listed Grade II as NHLE 1081040 under the entry name "Anti Air War Memorial". The socialist suffragist Sylvia Pankhurst commissioned and erected it in 1935 as "a protest against war in the air". It stands about 24 m from the IG8 0RD postcode unit on the open green and is visible at any hour. The two monuments are of directly opposed politics on one street.

St Mary's Church, on the High Road at E18 2QF, is the ancient parish church for Woodford and is listed Grade II as NHLE 1081032. It was in existence by the twelfth century, and its rector in the 1520s was John Larke. The medieval west tower and spire were dangerously decayed by 1705 and were replaced with a brick tower in 1708; the medieval church was substantially rebuilt in brick in Gothic style in 1816, and the church was rebuilt again in 1971-72 after an arson attack in 1969, so the interior is modern while the churchyard survives from the older building. It has a ring of eight bells cast at the Whitechapel Bell Foundry and a three-manual Grant, Degens and Bradbeer organ, and one of the Great Trees of London, a copper beech, stands in the churchyard. Four churchyard monuments carry their own entries, two of them at a higher grade than the church itself: the Godfrey Monument, Grade II*, NHLE 1357983, and the Raikes Mausoleum, Grade II*, NHLE 1183475, with the Keepe Monument, Grade II, NHLE 1081033, and the North Monument, Grade II, NHLE 1081034. No source states the church's opening hours, so none are given here.

Claybury Woods and Park, entered from Roding Lane North, IG8 8RW, covers over 70 hectares and held a Green Flag Award in 2024. Eighteen hectares of it are ancient oak and hornbeam woodland with veteran trees, fungi and woodland spring flowers including bluebells, and that woodland carries Forest Stewardship Council certification; the rest is extensive meadow, wildlife ponds, wetland and managed scrub, with a free outdoor gym. Claybury Hospital, on the ridge above the park, opened in 1893 as the fifth Middlesex County Asylum to designs by George Thomas Hine. Its main block, tower and chapel were listed Grade II on 13 June 1990 as NHLE 1080979; Claybury Hall was listed Grade II earlier, on 22 February 1979, as NHLE 1081005, and the former stable block at the hall is Grade II, NHLE 1300546. The hospital site has been redeveloped as housing and a gymnasium under the name Repton Park, with the former chapel now a swimming complex. The Claybury conservation area was designated in 2005, one of sixteen conservation areas in the borough.

sections.heading: Barkingside, Fairlop and Hainault
sections.body:
The Central line's Hainault loop runs up through Barkingside and Fairlop to Hainault, and the borough opens out into country parks along it.

Barnardo's Village stands on Tanners Lane, Barkingside, IG6 1QJ, 319 m from Barkingside station, and is the Barnardo's Village Homes conservation area, designated in 1990 and extended in November 2002. Thomas John Barnardo founded the charity in 1866 and it is still headquartered here. Six list entries sit inside the conservation area. Dr Barnardo's Memorial was listed on 22 February 1979 and upgraded to Grade II* on 20 May 2010, NHLE 1081001; George Frampton sculpted it without a fee and it was raised in 1908, three years after Barnardo's death in 1905, and his ashes were interred in front of Cairns House, the original building of the children's village. Twenty-two of the cottage homes were listed Grade II on 5 May 2010 under a single entry, NHLE 1393777, whose list name is "Twenty-two cottage homes at Barnardo's". The Children's Church and lych gate, NHLE 1393778, Cairns Cottage, NHLE 1393781, the fountain on the green, NHLE 1393779, and the lodge and boundary walls, NHLE 1393780, are each Grade II. Pert Cottages on the same lane carry two further Grade II entries, NHLE 1081010 for numbers 45-55 and NHLE 1357971 for numbers 33-43.

Fullwell Cross Library, at 140 High Street, Barkingside, IG6 2EA, was listed Grade II on 23 April 2007 as NHLE 1391938. Frederick Gibberd designed it circular, with a raised dome roof studded with sixteen-sided clerestory windows and finished in green copper, and Field Marshal Sir Gerald Templer, then Lieutenant of Greater London, opened it on 20 March 1968. It was refurbished in 2024 with funding from Vision, Redbridge Council and the Libraries Improvement Fund administered by Arts Council England. It is a working library, open Monday 10am to 8pm, Tuesday 10am to 6pm, Wednesday 10am to 8pm, Thursday 10am to 6pm and Saturday 10am to 5pm, and closed on Sunday; no source states a Friday time, so none is given here. It has two hireable halls, the Hainault Room and the larger Aldborough Room, and lends Hublet tablets for up to two hours at a time. Fairlop station is 507 m away and Barkingside station 851 m.

Hainault Forest Country Park is entered from Romford Road, Chigwell, IG7 4QN, a visitor address that falls in Redbridge; the park itself crosses into the London Borough of Havering and into the Lambourne parish of Epping Forest District in Essex. Hainault Forest was a large wooded area of Essex and Greater London, mostly destroyed after 1851, and public outrage at that destruction was an important catalyst for the modern environmental movement; less than a tenth of the original forest survives, much of it managed as this country park, and a small area was saved for public use in 1903. Published figures for its area differ — 136 hectares (340 acres) and 135.31 hectares (334.4 acres), the second given alongside a Site of Special Scientific Interest — and the adjoining Hainault Lodge Nature Reserve covers 6.8 hectares (17 acres). A £7m restoration rebuilt the Victorian barns as an events space, an interactive visitor hub, workshop units and the 1856 Cafe, with a new outdoor adventure play area; the cafe opens Monday to Sunday, 9am to 5pm. A Woodhenge behind the lake carries wood sculptures by local artists on a sculpture trail. Parking is paid through RingGo with no cash accepted: £1.80 for up to an hour, £3.10 for one to two hours and £6.40 all day.

Fairlop Waters Country Park, on Forest Road, Barkingside, IG6 3HN, is open space with two lakes and a golf course, laid out on former gravel workings on the site of Fairlop aerodrome. Its boulder park runs nine individual boulders of sprayed and carved concrete, varying in height and shape, all built for solo climbing and traversing from novice to expert. The large lake is used for sailing, rowing and windsurfing, and the Lakeside Suite in the Boathouse is licensed for weddings and civil ceremonies. In 2009 it was one of eleven parks across Greater London chosen by public vote for redevelopment funding, and it received £400,000 for footpaths, lighting, refurbished toilets and new play areas. Parking is £1.80 for up to an hour, £3.10 for one to two hours and £6.40 all day, and barbecues are not permitted. Fairlop station is 487 m from the visitor entrance and Hainault station about 1,010 m.

The Newbury Park station bus shelter, on Eastern Avenue, IG2 7RN, is a concrete-and-copper barrel vault designed by Oliver Hill, opened over the bus station beside the Underground entrance on 6 July 1949. It was listed Grade II on 19 March 1981 as NHLE 1081019, the entry amended on 30 July 2021, under the list name "Newbury Park Station Bus Shelter". The railway station beneath it was opened by the Great Eastern Railway on 1 May 1903; Underground trains began serving it on 14 December 1947 through the Gants Hill tunnel, and the line was extended to Hainault on 31 May 1948. Lifts giving step-free access were completed in November 2018, about ten years after Transport for London had abandoned the project. TfL records the bus station as a stop in its own right, naptanId 910GILFENBP, about 79 m from the Underground station stop, 940GZZLUNBP, and the shelter stands between the two, about 43 m from the Underground stop.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
Redbridge is a Central line borough with an Elizabeth line southern edge. Fourteen rail stations stand inside the boundary. Ten are London Underground Central line stations — Wanstead, Snaresbrook, South Woodford, Woodford, Redbridge, Gants Hill, Newbury Park, Barkingside, Fairlop and Hainault — and four are Elizabeth line stations on the Great Eastern main line: Ilford, Seven Kings, Goodmayes and Chadwell Heath, with Greater Anglia also calling at Ilford and Seven Kings. Chadwell Heath straddles the Redbridge and Barking and Dagenham boundary and belongs to both. There is no London Overground station, no DLR station, no tram stop and no District line station inside the borough; the nearest District line service is Barking, over the boundary in Barking and Dagenham. Two station buildings carry their own Grade II entries: Redbridge, NHLE 1401101, listed 20 July 2011 and opened on the new Hainault loop on 14 December 1947, and the western platform building at Barkingside, NHLE 1081012, listed 22 February 1979. Wanstead Park station, on the London Overground Suffragette line, is in Newham and about 2 km from Wanstead Park itself, so it is not the station for the park.

For Wanstead and Snaresbrook, take the Central line to Wanstead: 542 m from St Mary the Virgin on Overton Drive and about 1,270 m from the Temple. The City of London Corporation gives Wanstead Park — not the Temple specifically — as a 1 km (0.6 mile) walk from that station. Redbridge station is about 960 m from the Temple, and the Corporation gives the park as a 2.3 km (1.4 mile) walk from there. Snaresbrook is about 290 m from Snaresbrook Crown Court. The Corporation names the bus routes serving the area around the park: the 66, 101, 145, 308, W12, W13 and W14.

For Ilford, Gants Hill and Valentines, take the Elizabeth line or Greater Anglia to Ilford: about 400 m from Redbridge Museum in the Central Library, about 135 m from Ilford Hospital Chapel and 1,463 m from Valentines Mansion. Gants Hill, on the Central line, is 506 m from the mansion. Ilford is the borough's bus hub, with 24 routes stopping within 600 m of the town centre including the EL1 East London Transit and the SL2 Superloop, and 15 routes stop within 600 m of Valentines Mansion.

For Woodford, South Woodford and Claybury, take the Central line to South Woodford, 137 m from the South Woodford shops and the nearest station to St Mary's Church, or to Woodford, 1,084 m from the Churchill statue. Eight routes serve Woodford Green: the 20, 179, 275, 657, 675, 679, N55 and W13. Claybury has no station of its own: the nearest is Chigwell, another London Underground Central line station, 1,987 m from Claybury Hall and outside the borough in Epping Forest District, Essex, and three routes stop within 600 m of the park, the 169, the 275 and the W12. Highams Park, on the London Overground Weaver line, is 1,414 m from Woodford Green and stands in Waltham Forest.

For Barkingside, Fairlop and Hainault, take the Central line's Hainault loop. Barkingside is 319 m from Barnardo's Village and 851 m from Fullwell Cross Library; Fairlop is 507 m from the library and 487 m from Fairlop Waters; Hainault is about 1,010 m from Fairlop Waters. Ten routes stop in Barkingside town centre, and the 462 is the route stopping within 600 m of the Fairlop Waters entrance. No station is within walking distance of the Hainault Forest visitor centre at IG7 4QN: Grange Hill, a London Underground Central line station outside the borough in Essex, is about 850 m from the park's western boundary but about 3.0 km from the visitor centre, car park and 1856 Cafe, Hainault station is about 3.2 km from the same point, and the nearest bus stops are on Fowler Road about 840 m away, served by the 247 and the 362. Every distance here is a straight-line approximation, not a walking measurement.

faq.question: Which Underground and rail lines serve Redbridge?
faq.answer: Ten London Underground stations inside the borough are all on the Central line: Wanstead, Snaresbrook, South Woodford, Woodford, Redbridge, Gants Hill, Newbury Park, Barkingside, Fairlop and Hainault. Four Elizabeth line stations on the Great Eastern main line complete the fourteen rail stations inside the boundary — Ilford, Seven Kings, Goodmayes and Chadwell Heath — and Greater Anglia also calls at Ilford and Seven Kings. There is no London Overground station, no DLR, no tram and no District line station in the borough; the nearest District line service is Barking, over the boundary in Barking and Dagenham. Chadwell Heath straddles the Redbridge and Barking and Dagenham boundary.

faq.question: When is Valentines Mansion open, and does it cost anything?
faq.answer: Valentines Mansion, Emerson Road, Ilford, IG1 4XA, opens twice a week, on Sundays and Mondays: 12pm to 5pm from March to October and 11am to 3pm from November to February. Entry is free, and no dogs are admitted except guide dogs. The house was built in 1696 for Lady Tillotson, widow of John Tillotson, Archbishop of Canterbury, and was listed Grade II* on 10 April 1954 as NHLE 1081014. Vision RCL, a registered charity, manages it for Redbridge Council. Gants Hill station on the Central line is 506 m away and Ilford station 1,463 m.

faq.question: How do I get into the Temple in Wanstead Park?
faq.answer: The Temple, listed Grade II as NHLE 1081016, opens 11am to 3pm on published open days only. The City of London Corporation's 2026 dates are Sunday 15 March; Saturday 11 and Sunday 12 April; Saturday 25 and Sunday 26 April; Saturday 9 and Sunday 10 May; Saturday 13 and Sunday 14 June; Saturday 11 and Sunday 12 July; Saturday 8 and Sunday 9 August; Saturday 12 and Sunday 13 September; Sunday 11 October; Sunday 15 November; and Sunday 13 December. Entrance is free on those days and tours are available for a fee. It is reached from Warren Road, E11 2LT, where there is a small Blue Badge car park; Wanstead station is about 1,270 m away and Redbridge station about 960 m.

faq.question: How many listed buildings does Redbridge hold?
faq.answer: The National Heritage List for England records 138 listed-building entries inside the borough boundary: 1 at Grade I, 12 at Grade II* and 125 at Grade II. The Grade I entry is the Church of St Mary, Wanstead, NHLE 1081008. Two registered parks and gardens take the total to 140 — Wanstead Park at Grade II*, NHLE 1000194, covering 161.74 hectares, and Valentines Park at Grade II, NHLE 1000843, covering 51.52 hectares. Redbridge holds no scheduled monuments, no battlefields and no World Heritage Sites, and sixteen conservation areas are designated across the borough.

faq.question: What is there to do at Hainault Forest and Fairlop Waters?
faq.answer: Hainault Forest Country Park is entered from Romford Road, Chigwell, IG7 4QN, and crosses into Havering and into Essex. A £7m restoration rebuilt its Victorian barns as a visitor hub, workshop units, an events space and the 1856 Cafe, which opens Monday to Sunday, 9am to 5pm, with an outdoor adventure play area alongside. No station is within walking distance of that entrance: Grange Hill is about 3.0 km away and Hainault about 3.2 km, and the nearest bus stops are on Fowler Road about 840 m off, on the 247 and the 362. Fairlop Waters Country Park, Forest Road, IG6 3HN, is 487 m from Fairlop station and holds two lakes, a golf course and a boulder park of nine concrete boulders. Parking at both is £1.80 for an hour, £3.10 for two and £6.40 all day.

faq.question: Where is the borough's museum, and when does it open?
faq.answer: Redbridge Museum and Heritage Centre is on the second floor of Redbridge Central Library, Clements Road, Ilford, IG1 1EA, about 400 m from Ilford station. The museum opens Tuesday to Saturday, 11am to 5pm, and the Heritage Centre opens Tuesday to Friday and every other Saturday, 10.30am to 4pm. Arts Council England records one Accredited museum inside the borough: this one holds Full Accreditation, with Vision Redbridge Culture & Leisure as its governing body. Its permanent exhibition reopened in August 2024 after a redevelopment, and the collection covers over 200,000 years of Redbridge history.

places.name: Wanstead Park

The managed municipal park inside the registered boundary is about 140 acres, or 57 hectares. The Corporation publishes no general opening hours for it, so none are given here.

places.name: The Grotto, Wanstead Park
places.address: Wanstead Park, Warren Road, Wanstead, London E11 2LT
places.summary: The Grotto stands on the bank of the Ornamental Waters in Wanstead Park, about 270 m from the E11 2LT postcode unit, and is listed Grade II as NHLE 1183624. It is a roofless shell, seen from the lakeside path rather than entered.

Redbridge holds no scheduled monuments, and garden buildings of this kind carry much of the borough's older fabric instead.

places.name: Church of St Mary the Virgin, Wanstead
places.summary: The Church of St Mary the Virgin is a working Anglican parish church on Overton Drive, Wanstead, E11 2LW, listed Grade I as NHLE 1081008; the National Heritage List for England records one Grade I entry inside the borough and this is it. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.

places.history: The Grade II listing was made on 11 November 1968 as list entry 1358004 and amended on 12 December 2019. George Gilbert Scott and William Bonython Moffatt built it in 1841-1843 in Jacobean Gothic for the Infant Orphan Asylum, founded by the philanthropist Andrew Reed. It remained an orphanage until 1938, then the Royal Wanstead School until 1971, and was converted to a Crown Court for £1.6m in 1973, opening as a court on 26 November 1974. It is a third-tier centre and one of twelve serving Greater London. The former gatekeeper's lodge, NHLE 1467326, and the former indoor swimming pool, NHLE 1467344, were both added to the list at Grade II on 3 December 2019, fifty-one years after the main building. Snaresbrook station is about 290 m away.

places.name: Valentines Mansion and Gardens
places.summary: Valentines Mansion stands on Emerson Road, Ilford, IG1 4XA, is listed Grade II* as NHLE 1081014 and sits in the Valentines Mansion conservation area. Entry is free and the operator opens the house twice a week, on Sundays and Mondays: 12pm to 5pm from March to October and 11am to 3pm from November to February. No dogs are admitted except guide dogs.
places.history: The Grade II* listing was made on 10 April 1954 as list entry 1081014. The house was built in 1696 for Lady Tillotson, widow of John Tillotson, Archbishop of Canterbury, and Vision RCL, the registered charity that manages it for Redbridge Council, describes over 320 years of history on the site. The period rooms shown to visitors include the Drawing Room, Morning Room, Regency Parlour, Bedchamber, Victorian Kitchen and Grand Staircase, and the grounds hold the Old English Garden and the Walled Garden, with the Gardener's Cottage Cafe beside the house. Seven further structures in the immediate grounds carry their own entries at two different grades: the railings, gates and gatepiers to Valentines Park are Grade II*, NHLE 1081027, while the dovecote and attached garden walls, NHLE 1081015, the canal-head grotto, NHLE 1183617, a second grotto, NHLE 1244052, the ha-ha, NHLE 1244054, the sundial, NHLE 1244053, and the Gardener's Cottage, NHLE 1360821, are each Grade II. Gants Hill station is 506 m away and Ilford station 1,463 m.

places.name: Valentines Park
places.summary: Valentines Park is a Grade II registered park and garden of 51.52 hectares, NHLE 1000843, entered from Cranbrook Road, Ilford, IG1 4TG. It was laid out as the grounds of Valentines Mansion and holds a Green Flag Award, a 300-year-old field maple, ornamental gardens, flowering meadows, two children's play areas and two cafes — the Gardener's Cottage Cafe by the mansion and Valentines Park Cafe by the bandstand.
places.history: The park was registered at Grade II on 1 October 1987 as list entry 1000843, and Historic England records the registered area as 51.52 hectares. Its boundary railings, gates and gatepiers were listed Grade II* in their own right on 10 April 1954, NHLE 1081027, a higher grade than the park's registration. Two grottoes inside it, NHLE 1183617 and NHLE 1244052, and the ha-ha, NHLE 1244054, are Grade II. The outdoor gym carries 15 pieces of equipment across 20 work stations. Gants Hill station on the Central line is the nearest Underground station to the mansion at 506 m.

places.name: Redbridge Museum and Heritage Centre
places.address: Second floor, Redbridge Central Library, Clements Road, Ilford IG1 1EA
places.summary: Redbridge Museum and Heritage Centre occupies the second floor of Redbridge Central Library, Clements Road, Ilford, IG1 1EA, about 400 m from Ilford station. The museum opens Tuesday to Saturday, 11am to 5pm; the Heritage Centre opens Tuesday to Friday and every other Saturday, 10.30am to 4pm.
places.history: Arts Council England records one Accredited museum inside the borough: this one holds Full Accreditation, with Vision Redbridge Culture & Leisure as its governing body and Local Authority as its museum type. The museum states that it explores "the many different places, people and events in over 200,000 years of Redbridge history", and its permanent exhibition reopened in August 2024 after a redevelopment. The Heritage Centre is the borough's archive and local studies service, holding material on the history of Ilford, Wanstead, Woodford and Redbridge with free local and family history resources.

places.name: Ilford Hospital Chapel
places.summary: Ilford Hospital Chapel, formally the Hospital Chapel of St Mary the Virgin and St Thomas of Canterbury, stands on Ilford Hill above the Roding at IG1 2AT and is listed Grade II* as NHLE 1300587. It is an almshouse foundation dating from about 1130. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: The Grade II* listing was made on 10 April 1954 as list entry 1300587 and amended on 20 June 2003. The almshouses, NHLE 1390507, and the chaplain's house, NHLE 1390508, were added to the list at Grade II on 20 June 2003, nearly fifty years after the chapel itself. The chapel stands about 22 m from the IG1 2AT postcode unit and about 135 m south of Ilford station, which is served by the Elizabeth line and Greater Anglia.

places.name: Statue of Winston Churchill, Woodford Green
places.address: Woodford Green, High Road, Woodford Green IG8 9HF
places.summary: The Statue of Winston Churchill stands on the open green beside the High Road at Woodford Green, IG8 9HF, and is listed Grade II as NHLE 1430402 under the entry name "Statue of Winston Churchill (and plinth)". The green is open at any hour.
places.history: The Grade II listing was made on 19 January 2016 as list entry 1430402. David McFall made the bronze in 1958-59 and it was erected in 1959. It commemorates Churchill's service as member for the Woodford constituency: he was elected for Epping in 1924, held the new Woodford seat from 1945 and stood down in 1964. Sylvia Pankhurst's Anti-Air War Memorial, Grade II, NHLE 1081040, stands about 1.5 km north along the same High Road. Woodford station is 1,084 m away and South Woodford 1,464 m.

places.name: Anti-Air War Memorial, Woodford Green
places.summary: The Anti-Air War Memorial is a stone bomb on a plinth standing on the open green beside the High Road at IG8 0RD, listed Grade II as NHLE 1081040 under the entry name "Anti Air War Memorial". It is about 24 m from the IG8 0RD postcode unit and is visible at any hour.
places.history: The socialist suffragist Sylvia Pankhurst commissioned and erected it in 1935 as "a protest against war in the air". It faces the Statue of Winston Churchill, Grade II, NHLE 1430402, about 1.5 km south along the same High Road: two monuments of directly opposed politics on one street. The Grade II listing is list entry 1081040.

places.name: St Mary's Church, Woodford
places.address: High Road, Woodford Green, London E18 2QF
places.summary: St Mary's Church is the ancient parish church for Woodford, on the High Road at E18 2QF, listed Grade II as NHLE 1081032. The interior is modern, rebuilt after a fire in 1969, while the churchyard and its monuments survive from the older building. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: The Grade II listing is list entry 1081032. The church was in existence by the twelfth century and its rector in the 1520s was John Larke. The medieval west tower and spire were dangerously decayed by 1705 and were replaced with a brick tower in 1708; the medieval church was substantially rebuilt in brick in Gothic style in 1816, and the church was rebuilt again in 1971-72 after an arson attack in 1969. It has a ring of eight bells cast at the Whitechapel Bell Foundry and a three-manual Grant, Degens and Bradbeer organ, and one of the Great Trees of London, a copper beech, stands in the churchyard. Four churchyard monuments carry their own entries, two of them at a higher grade than the church itself: the Godfrey Monument, Grade II*, NHLE 1357983, and the Raikes Mausoleum, Grade II*, NHLE 1183475, with the Keepe Monument, Grade II, NHLE 1081033, and the North Monument, Grade II, NHLE 1081034. South Woodford station is the nearest station.

places.name: Claybury Woods and Park
places.address: Roding Lane North, Woodford Green IG8 8RW
places.summary: Claybury Woods and Park covers over 70 hectares off Roding Lane North, IG8 8RW, and held a Green Flag Award in 2024. Eighteen hectares of it are ancient oak and hornbeam woodland with veteran trees, fungi and woodland spring flowers including bluebells, and the rest is meadow, wildlife ponds, wetland and managed scrub, with a free outdoor gym. It lies in the Claybury conservation area.
places.history: The ancient woodland carries Forest Stewardship Council certification. Claybury Hospital, on the ridge above the park, opened in 1893 as the fifth Middlesex County Asylum to designs by George Thomas Hine; its main block, tower and chapel were listed Grade II on 13 June 1990 as NHLE 1080979. Claybury Hall was listed Grade II earlier, on 22 February 1979, as NHLE 1081005, and the former stable block at the hall is Grade II, NHLE 1300546. The hospital site has been redeveloped as housing and a gymnasium under the name Repton Park, with the former chapel now a swimming complex. The Claybury conservation area was designated in 2005, one of sixteen in the borough. Chigwell station on the Central line, 1,987 m from Claybury Hall, is the nearest station and stands outside the borough in Epping Forest District, Essex; the 169, the 275 and the W12 stop within 600 m of the park.

places.name: Barnardo's Village, Barkingside
places.summary: Barnardo's Village on Tanners Lane, Barkingside, IG6 1QJ, is the Barnardo's Village Homes conservation area, designated in 1990 and extended in November 2002, with six list entries inside it. Thomas John Barnardo founded the charity in 1866 and it is still headquartered here. Barkingside station is 319 m from the village green.
places.history: Dr Barnardo's Memorial was listed on 22 February 1979 and upgraded to Grade II* on 20 May 2010, NHLE 1081001. George Frampton sculpted it without a fee and it was raised in 1908, three years after Barnardo's death in 1905; his ashes were interred in front of Cairns House, the original building of the children's village. Twenty-two of the cottage homes were listed Grade II on 5 May 2010 under a single entry, NHLE 1393777, whose list name is "Twenty-two cottage homes at Barnardo's". The Children's Church and lych gate, NHLE 1393778, Cairns Cottage, NHLE 1393781, the fountain on the green, NHLE 1393779, and the lodge and boundary walls, NHLE 1393780, are each Grade II. Pert Cottages on the same lane carry two further Grade II entries, NHLE 1081010 for numbers 45-55 and NHLE 1357971 for numbers 33-43.

places.name: Fullwell Cross Library
places.summary: Fullwell Cross Library, at 140 High Street, Barkingside, IG6 2EA, is a circular building by Frederick Gibberd with a raised dome roof studded with sixteen-sided clerestory windows and finished in green copper, listed Grade II as NHLE 1391938. It is a working library, open Monday 10am to 8pm, Tuesday 10am to 6pm, Wednesday 10am to 8pm, Thursday 10am to 6pm and Saturday 10am to 5pm, and closed on Sunday; no source states a Friday time, so none is given here.
places.history: The Grade II listing was made on 23 April 2007 as list entry 1391938. Field Marshal Sir Gerald Templer, then Lieutenant of Greater London, opened the building on 20 March 1968. It was refurbished in 2024 with funding from Vision, Redbridge Council and the Libraries Improvement Fund administered by Arts Council England. It has two hireable halls, the Hainault Room and the larger Aldborough Room, and lends Hublet tablets for up to two hours at a time. Fairlop station is 507 m away and Barkingside station 851 m, both on the Central line's Hainault loop.

places.name: Hainault Forest Country Park
places.address: Hainault Forest Country Park, Romford Road, Chigwell IG7 4QN
places.summary: Hainault Forest Country Park is entered from Romford Road, Chigwell, IG7 4QN, a visitor address that falls in Redbridge; the park crosses into the London Borough of Havering and into the Lambourne parish of Epping Forest District in Essex. The 1856 Cafe in the rebuilt Victorian barns opens Monday to Sunday, 9am to 5pm. Parking is paid through RingGo with no cash accepted: £1.80 for up to an hour, £3.10 for one to two hours and £6.40 all day.
places.history: Hainault Forest was a large wooded area of Essex and Greater London, mostly destroyed after 1851, and public outrage at that destruction was an important catalyst for the modern environmental movement; less than a tenth of the original forest survives, much of it managed as this country park, and a small area was saved for public use in 1903. Published figures for the country park's area differ — 136 hectares (340 acres) and 135.31 hectares (334.4 acres), the second given alongside a Site of Special Scientific Interest — and the adjoining Hainault Lodge Nature Reserve covers 6.8 hectares (17 acres). A £7m restoration rebuilt the Victorian barns as an events space, an interactive visitor hub, workshop units and the 1856 Cafe, with a new outdoor adventure play area. A Woodhenge behind the lake carries wood sculptures by local artists on a sculpture trail. No station stands within walking distance of the visitor centre: Grange Hill, in Essex, is about 3.0 km from it and Hainault about 3.2 km, and the nearest bus stops are on Fowler Road about 840 m away, on the 247 and the 362.

places.name: Fairlop Waters Country Park
places.address: Fairlop Waters Country Park, Forest Road, Barkingside IG6 3HN
places.summary: Fairlop Waters Country Park, on Forest Road, Barkingside, IG6 3HN, is open space with two lakes and a golf course, laid out on former gravel workings on the site of Fairlop aerodrome. Its boulder park runs nine individual boulders of sprayed and carved concrete, varying in height and shape, all built for solo climbing and traversing from novice to expert. Parking is £1.80 for up to an hour, £3.10 for one to two hours and £6.40 all day, and barbecues are not permitted.
places.history: The large lake is used for sailing, rowing and windsurfing, and the Lakeside Suite in the Boathouse is licensed for weddings and civil ceremonies. In 2009 the park was one of eleven across Greater London chosen by public vote for redevelopment funding, and it received £400,000 for footpaths, lighting, refurbished toilets and new play areas. Fairlop station is 487 m from the visitor entrance and Hainault station about 1,010 m, both on the Central line's Hainault loop; within 600 m of the IG6 3HN entrance the 462 is the route that stops, while nine routes call at Fairlop station about 500 m away.

places.name: Newbury Park Station Bus Shelter
places.address: Eastern Avenue, Newbury Park, Ilford IG2 7RN
places.summary: The Newbury Park station bus shelter is a concrete-and-copper barrel vault by Oliver Hill standing over the bus station on Eastern Avenue, IG2 7RN, beside the Underground entrance. It opened on 6 July 1949 and is listed Grade II as NHLE 1081019. It stands over a working bus station and is seen from the street at any hour.
places.history: The Grade II listing was made on 19 March 1981 as list entry 1081019 and amended on 30 July 2021, under the list name "Newbury Park Station Bus Shelter". The railway station beneath it was opened by the Great Eastern Railway on 1 May 1903; Underground trains began serving it on 14 December 1947 through the Gants Hill tunnel, and the line was extended to Hainault on 31 May 1948. Newbury Park is on the Central line's Hainault loop between Gants Hill and Barkingside, in fare zone 4, and lifts giving step-free access were completed in November 2018, about ten years after Transport for London had abandoned the project. TfL records the bus station as a stop in its own right, naptanId 910GILFENBP, about 79 m from the Underground station stop, 940GZZLUNBP; the shelter stands between the two, about 43 m from the Underground stop.

links.note: Hainault Forest Country Park crosses the shared edge into Havering, and the Central line's Hainault loop runs along it; Havering has no Central line station.
One forest under one Conservator since 1878: Wanstead Park is Redbridge's and Chingford Plain is Waltham Forest's, with the boundary running through Bush Wood.
The Roding runs down into Newham, and Wanstead Flats is the Epping Forest land that continues south from Redbridge's Wanstead into the borough next door.
Valentines Park is a Grade II registered park and garden, NHLE 1000843, on the shared boundary; Barking and Dagenham holds no registered landscape of its own.

entries.name: Wanstead Park
entries.note: A Grade II* registered park and garden of 161.74 hectares, NHLE 1000194, that the City of London Corporation has administered as part of Epping Forest since 1880.

entries.name: The Temple, Wanstead Park
entries.note: An Epping Forest visitor centre listed Grade II as NHLE 1081016, open 11am to 3pm on published dates, free entrance, with the park's Roman villa told in mosaics.

entries.name: The Grotto, Wanstead Park
entries.note: A roofless garden structure of the Wanstead House estate on the bank of the Ornamental Waters, listed Grade II as NHLE 1183624 and seen from the lakeside path.

entries.name: Church of St Mary the Virgin, Wanstead
entries.note: Thomas Hardwick's church of 1787-90 on Overton Drive, listed Grade I as NHLE 1081008, with its gatepiers Grade II*, NHLE 1081022.

entries.name: Snaresbrook Crown Court
entries.note: Scott and Moffatt's orphanage of 1841-43, listed Grade II as NHLE 1358004, a working court of 20 rooms read from Hollybush Hill above Eagle Pond.

entries.name: Valentines Mansion and Gardens
entries.note: A house of 1696 listed Grade II* as NHLE 1081014, free to enter on Sundays and Mondays, 12pm to 5pm March to October and 11am to 3pm November to February.

entries.name: Valentines Park
entries.note: A Grade II registered park and garden of 51.52 hectares, NHLE 1000843, whose railings and gatepiers are Grade II* in their own right, NHLE 1081027.

entries.name: Redbridge Museum and Heritage Centre
entries.note: Tuesday to Saturday, 11am to 5pm on the second floor of the Central Library; the Heritage Centre opens Tuesday to Friday and every other Saturday, 10.30am to 4pm.

entries.name: Ilford Hospital Chapel
entries.note: An almshouse foundation of about 1130 on Ilford Hill, listed Grade II* as NHLE 1300587, with its almshouses Grade II, NHLE 1390507.

entries.name: Statue of Winston Churchill, Woodford Green
entries.note: David McFall's bronze of 1958-59, erected 1959 on the green beside the High Road and listed Grade II as NHLE 1430402.

entries.name: Anti-Air War Memorial, Woodford Green
entries.note: Sylvia Pankhurst's stone bomb of 1935, listed Grade II as NHLE 1081040, facing the Churchill statue 1.5 km down the same High Road.

entries.name: St Mary's Church, Woodford
entries.note: The ancient parish church, listed Grade II as NHLE 1081032, with a churchyard holding two Grade II* monuments, NHLE 1357983 and NHLE 1183475.

entries.name: Claybury Woods and Park
entries.note: Over 70 hectares off Roding Lane North with 18 hectares of ancient oak and hornbeam woodland, below the Grade II hospital block of 1893, NHLE 1080979.

entries.name: Barnardo's Village, Barkingside
entries.note: A conservation area of 1990 around Frampton's Grade II* memorial of 1908, NHLE 1081001, and twenty-two cottage homes under one Grade II entry, NHLE 1393777.

entries.name: Fullwell Cross Library
entries.note: Frederick Gibberd's circular library of 1968 under a green copper dome, listed Grade II as NHLE 1391938 and still a working lending library.

entries.name: Hainault Forest Country Park
entries.note: The surviving tenth of the old forest, with rebuilt Victorian barns and the 1856 Cafe open 9am to 5pm daily; parking £1.80 an hour, £6.40 all day.

entries.name: Fairlop Waters Country Park
entries.note: Two lakes and a golf course on the old Fairlop aerodrome, with nine concrete bouldering blocks, 487 m from Fairlop station; barbecues are not permitted.

entries.name: Newbury Park Station Bus Shelter
entries.note: Oliver Hill's concrete-and-copper barrel vault of 6 July 1949 over the bus station, listed Grade II as NHLE 1081019.
